## Details

### elektron-firmware-tool

C, MIT licence. Unpacks Elektron .syx firmware and repacks it as a valid file. Lists Analog Heat MKI, MKII and +FX among supported devices - currently the only Analog Heat-relevant tool we found. Forum listing: 113 stars, repo created 2026-07-22, "last commit 1 month ago" at the time of listing.

_Sources: forum mod list (mods.php?id=7), forum thread 8_

### Overtone

Python 3.11+ patcher (patcher/patch.py) that builds Overtone from the user's own OS 1.12 and only saves the result if it matches the tested build byte for byte; install via Elektron Transfer over USB. Adds machines SOPHIE, MACHINEDRUM, LOOP, THRU, per-track insert effects, envelope followers, two arpeggiators, parameter slides and GROOVE (replaces swing). 1.0.1 fixes installing an OS sent with Transfer while Overtone runs. About 160 checks per build in two emulators (digikit for the main OS, a SHARC emulator for the DSP program); author states 1.0.1 passes all of them, is played on a Digitone II and Transfer installs were checked on the unit. Opening Overtone projects on stock OS is untested. Recovery section is detailed (FUNC + TRIG 4, DIN MIDI, ~15 min). AGPL-3.0-or-later (includes dnfw), 5 commits. Related: dnfw, digikit, dn2-cfw, Schwung Sophie (MIT), and the author's digitone-2-modding-skill used with Claude Code.

_Latest seen (2026-10-31, secondary directories): altstrument: v1.1 (2026-10-30) reworks GROOVE with presets, a random drift control, random weights and arrow-key editing, and restores FUNC + TEMPO as tap tempo; v1.0.1 (2026-10-29) fixes installing Elektron's OS or an Overtone update with Transfer while Overtone runs._

_Related: uses tool `digikit` (catalogue notes: checks run in digikit for the main OS); cites `digisophie` (README credits: Schwung Sophie for the SOPHIE machine); vendors `dn2-firmware-explore` (README: patcher/_dnfw is dnfw's code, unchanged); cites `dn2-cfw` (README: dn2-cfw showed how to ship Digitone II firmware); uses tool `digitone-2-modding-skill` (README: developed with the digitone-2-modding-skill) - see [PROJECT-FAMILIES.md](../PROJECT-FAMILIES.md)_

_Sources: forum thread 90, GitHub README_

### x0x (808/909 kick machines)

808 and 909 kick machines (MODEL 0 = 808, 127 = 909; TNTUN, DECAY, ATTK) that use the device's own sequencer, filters, AMP and effects, built from the user's stock OS for each device. On the Digitone II a new kick fades the previous one on the same track over about 2.7 ms. Physical qualification on Digitakt and Digitone is in progress (issue 94). docs/dn2-remote-control.md drives a DN2 1.12 remotely through a DigiHealth helper (remote keys, screen frames, ColdFire and DSP peek). Licence file not found in the clone. Found by GitHub code search 2026-11-03.

_Sources: GitHub code search 2026-11-03, README, docs/dn2-remote-control.md_

### DigiRust

macOS patcher, "experimental Digitone II tools", use at own risk. Features include drone latch and Perform Kit restoration (see docs/FEATURES.md in the repo). Creates a verified copy locally, never talks to the instrument.

_Sources: GitHub release v1.2.0_

### SYXGRID v2

Free browser-based pattern/sequence editor, not a firmware mod. Repo includes sysexmap/, a public reverse-engineered SysEx format map (CC BY 4.0): 45 mappings, map version 1.13.0, each with a confidence level (A = hardware-confirmed on a DN2: 23; B = corpus-confirmed by repo fixtures: 12; C = inherited, one value exercised: 9; D = unknown, do not rely: 1). Narrowed by bisection on 2026-09-08 against a Digitone II (OS 1.10E) and a Digitakt II. Not decoded: parameter locks, sound parameters (filter, amp, FX, LFO), synth machine choice. Needs the DN2 in SYSEX RECEIVE mode; Web MIDI needs Chromium over HTTPS or localhost (Chrome/Edge 152 break SysEx receive on macOS). App is AGPLv3 since v22.46 (MIT through v22.37). 6 commits.

_Related: uses tool `digikit` (README: checks or gates run in digikit's emulator (not shipped)); cites `digi-roll` (README: its DN2 pattern-format documentation); cites `dn2-firmware-explore` (README: cited throughout its maps; its code is not used); cites `elektroid` (README: reference for Elektron device transfer over USB); cites `libanalogrytm` (README: reference for Elektron structures); cites `dnx` (README: its published hardware measurements); cites `digitone-syx-toolkit` (README: used as cross-reference / prior art); vendors `elk-herd` (README credits under Code: elk-herd, BSD-2-Clause) - see [PROJECT-FAMILIES.md](../PROJECT-FAMILIES.md)_

### DN2 DT2 firmware research

Source-only recipes for Digitone II firmware with six Digitakt II sample machines (ONESHOT, WERP, STRETCH, REPITCH, GRID, SLICE), stereo samples, sample browsing, DT2 parameter graphics and SLICES trig mode. Recorder adds recording/resampling, source selection, normalization, trimming, audition, saving to +Drive and optional track assignment; VOICE cycles Voice Setup, Sample Manager and Recorder. Class-compliant USB audio provides 42 capture channels at 48 kHz/24 bit (MAIN, tracks 1-16, DELAY, REVERB, CHORUS, INPUT as stereo pairs) and a stereo return. R012 needs only the official DN2 1.11 and DT2 1.16 OS files; silent compatibility data replaces the private sample bank, and users load their own playable samples afterward. Native and browser builders verify exact inputs and the output: 2,563,872 bytes, SHA-256 4a2742a4...63a3a9a. The browser builds locally without uploading files; neither builder flashes the instrument. No firmware images or samples are distributed. Historical exact T1E2/R003/R008/R011 builds still require their original private sample bank. R011 fixed USB publication stalling after project changes by selecting its candidate destination from current DMA START while preserving ownership checks; R012 retains that fix. Owner-confirmed stock audio, samples, Recorder and USB audio on R012, including after project changes. Stable does not mean exhaustive validation: exact trimmed-file comparison, full Recorder-source coverage, endurance and end-to-end USB latency remain unverified. Builds on dnfw (angellinares/dn2_firmware_explore), selache, digikit and elektron-firmware-tool. AGPL-3.0-or-later. 2026-11-03: README warns new users NOT to install R012 yet. R012 mounts an existing sample filesystem but does not create one on a DN2 that never had it; symptoms are 0% Free / 0 bytes in Transfer, stalled uploads, Connection failed. The author says stock FORMAT +DRIVE, EMPTY RESET and FACTORY RESET do not create it and can erase projects; at that point an on-device formatter was still in development. R013 subsequently added FORMAT SAMPLES with erase confirmation; formatting, restart, capacity and post-format uploads were checked on the owner's unit. Owner testing of R012 had used storage prepared during development. An earlier track-2 saved-project reload report was an unsaved checkpoint; R022 addresses a separate, reproduced failure to refresh the sample table in the unsaved working-state backup. This does not establish recovery from an interrupted write or USB freeze.

_Related: builds on `dn2-firmware-explore` (catalogue notes: builds on dnfw (pinned commit)); builds on `digikit` (catalogue notes: builds on digikit (pinned commit)); builds on `elektron-firmware-tool` (catalogue notes: builds on elektron-firmware-tool (pinned commit)) - see [PROJECT-FAMILIES.md](../PROJECT-FAMILIES.md)_

### digikit

Native Rust emulator that runs the ColdFire and SHARC+ firmware together, with front panel, display and audio, plus a web panel (WASM core), a Tauri desktop app, the patch toolchain "patchkit" (applies modules to the user's own .syx), a headless scenario runner with pinned PCM hashes, a control socket for patch injection and DSP/ColdFire analysis databases with Ghidra tooling. README caveats: the DSP "does not run in real time yet", the browser host is parked on branch wip/browser-host, "no patched firmware has been installed on a device", and recovery via the bootstrap menu is "not tested on hardware". patchkit refuses to change sections 2, 4 and 8. 982 commits, AGPL-3.0-or-later with extra section-7 terms (attribution, origin, names) in NOTICE; page shows 46 open issues. GitHub marks it as not a fork. The org ElekLabs has 2 public repos: digikit and a fork of js216/selache. Original author: the GitHub profile m-dwyer is named "Em D" (Melbourne), which is exactly the credit ElekLabs' NOTICE requires ("digikit by Em D"); Overtone credits digikit to "Em D" as well. The earlier repo m-dwyer/digikit (196 commits, 4 stars, GPL-2.0-or-later, README at the time: "no audio", last visible file HANDOVER-2026-09-16) shows no move/archive notice and does not mention ElekLabs. ElekLabs has no public members, so the pages themselves do not show who runs it; the maintainer (user of this repo) states that Em D develops in ElekLabs/digikit (2026-10-31, not verifiable on the pages). The licence changed from GPL-2.0-or-later to AGPL-3.0-or-later with extra terms. Treat both repos as one project line, ElekLabs/digikit being the current one. Mod READMEs that say "digikit's emulator" mean this project.

_Latest seen (2026-10-31, secondary directories): altstrument (2026-10-31): main @ 283bb90, untagged, described as patch toolchain AND run-time module system plus emulator; AGPL-3.0-or-later. Its device-side tools (dkupload, dklog) belong to that module system._

_Related: cites `elektron-firmware-tool` (README: container-format knowledge comes from elektron-firmware-tool); cites `dt2-firmware-research` (README: some architecture facts come from lalzart/digitakt-ii-firmware-research-public) - see [PROJECT-FAMILIES.md](../PROJECT-FAMILIES.md)_

_Sources: GitHub README ElekLabs/digikit, GitHub README m-dwyer/digikit, lapin-list_

### dn2_firmware_explore

Tools to inspect, modify and rebuild Digitone firmware (dnfw, CLI and browser), plus 17 mods for Digitone II 1.11 (Waverider wavetable machine, LFO4, arp modes, LFO waves, FX destinations and others), each with a version and a changelog. The ~80% recovery-path stall once listed as open was the MIDI link, not the image (settled 2026-09-11). AGPL-3.0-or-later.

_Latest seen (2026-10-31, secondary directories): altstrument: OS 1.11 target; includes the dnfw inspect/modify/rebuild tool, which also runs in the browser. Hardware-confirmed mods: lfo4, arpmodes, lfowaves, midiarp, layermidi, fxmod and the lfolength fix (2026-10-09, audio track). No GitHub releases - tags are work snapshots._

### dn2-cfw

Public lab notebook: notes, tools and new effects, no Elektron firmware included. Seven builds run on real hardware per README (EF01 renamed stock, FLG1 flanger replacing the chorus, FTD1 + one-head tape delay, DH01 core/hook bus with a MIDI test mod, FTN1 renamed screens, GT00 parameter table moved, GT01 + 17 hidden rows for the 3-band compressor); not yet on the unit: the 3-band compressor and a Space-Echo-style delay (fx/spaceecho.c). Rule of the author: "nothing counts as working until it has run on my unit". Getting started (README): macOS on Apple silicon (Linux likely for most), Python 3, the user's own Digitone_II_OS1_12.syx in elektron-firmware/, upstream tools cloned into vendor/ (VENDOR.md) - for digikit and elekloader the author's forks on branch dn2-1.12 (digikit: 1.12 support, audio clock, DIN MIDI, LEDs, live play; elekloader: Digitone II 1.12 profile and the core-dn2 hook bus), commands scripts/dn2-emu-112.sh all, scripts/dn2-live.sh, fx make test/renders, tools/brickcheck/brickcheck CANDIDATE.syx (12 checks, must pass before any flash). README gives no step-by-step flashing procedure. Docs: ROADMAP.md, HANDOFF.md (later entries supersede earlier), FIRMWARE.md (sha256s), VENDOR.md, docs/parameter-table-growth.md, notes/ (one report per task, claims marked [verified] or [inferred]), analysis/ (class hierarchy recovered from RTTI). 28 commits, GPL-2.0(-or-later).

_Latest seen (2026-10-31, secondary directories): Renamed Digiwerk (altstrument; stock OS 1.12, GPL-2.0-or-later, notarized Mac patcher app). v0.1.0 (2026-10-26): Deja vu LFO waves and the Compressor + Flanger pack (build DJ01). v0.2.0 (2026-10-29): key-following LFO wave, one-cycle and half-cycle LFO modes, SHUF/RAND/TM arp modes (also on MIDI tracks), a tape echo, per-slot effect choice. v0.2.1 (2026-10-30): withdraws the six spring-reverb builds - the page says the CFES and EFTS builds stop the sound on a Digitone II - and removes the spring tile from the patcher; the other eight builds are unchanged._

_Related: vendors `digikit` (catalogue notes: upstream cloned into vendor/ (author's fork, branch dn2-1.12)); vendors `elekloader` (catalogue notes: upstream cloned into vendor/ (author's fork, branch dn2-1.12)); cites `elektron-firmware-tool` (README credits); cites `syntakt-firmware-workbench` (README: the Syntakt Firmware Workbench as behavioural reference); cites `octabam` (README: ColdFire disassembly findings / credits); vendors `digitakt-ii-research` (README: Kari Gardarsson's Deja vu LFO from the Digitakt II, brought to the Digitone II) - see [PROJECT-FAMILIES.md](../PROJECT-FAMILIES.md)_

### Elektroid

### DN2 mk2 Mod (dn2mk2-firmware)

Adds Digitakt II sample machines (ONESHOT, WERP, STRETCH, REPITCH, GRID, SLICE) with sample browser and recorder, PERC (34 Machinedrum machines incl. TRX, EFM, GND, P-I), Monomachine voices (SID 6581, DPRO WAVE/DDRW/DENS, VO-6) and a CPU guard. Browser-based patcher builds from the user's own files ("nothing is uploaded") and saves only if the output sha256 matches a build that passed scripts/ship_gate.py. Hardware: README says verification is pending per version; FIRMWARE.md says nearly every v0.21-v0.33 entry was checked in emulators and "not seen on hardware yet". Main open problem: DSP time (heavy voices cut sound). Flashing a 1.12 unit takes it back to a 1.11 base, projects saved under the newer OS may not open. 1,491 commits, 8 stars, AGPL-3.0-or-later. FIRMWARE.md says built firmware is kept on the repo's `builds` branch (not main) - unlike most projects here, which only ship patchers; we link only to the repo and docs, not to builds. Withdrawn builds: v0.4-v0.7 (oversized image). v0.38 (2026-11-02): Direct Jump state kept in its own +Drive sector (0x6FF000); per-project sample lists at +Drive 0x6D0000-0x6E02FF, two checked copies each. Root cause of the silent new samples: the DSP plays a pool slot only below the directory's count, and live adds did not update the count. v0.39 (2026-11-03): recordings had kept only ~2 ms since v0.38 because the DSP recorder took words 2-4 of every new link command as source, channel and threshold, and v0.38 sent a check command at every take's start; now only the recorder's own commands set them.

_Latest seen (2026-10-31, secondary directories): v0.34 TIMING: P-I voices that stayed dead after v0.33's guard muted them are now reset on the next note; a FUNC-held readout shows V1D (bad data in a voice's delay memory) or V1X (elsewhere); new USB diag tool tools/dn2diag.py reads the guard record and scans DSP memory for bad values; the ColdFire emulator now fires the audio interrupt at its real rate, and DSP tests charge memory like the chip. v0.35 SWEEP (2026-11-01): fixes only (MACHINE SEL filter list, +DRIVE preview retrigger, SYN-held values, LOAD TO PROJ, deleted folders, LFO page names). Open: why P-I / VO-6 voices go bad on the instrument. Same scope as armio's T1E2 (DT2 sample machines on DN2 1.11). v0.36 VOICES: the fixed two-voice cap on Monomachine tracks is gone (the real-time DSP guard decides): SID, VO-6, DENS and DPRO WAVE play 4-note chords, DDRW 2; when there is no room the oldest voice is dropped cleanly; DDRW/DENS tables moved to fast memory; a Diagnostics section in the import page reads the instrument after a silent voice. ROADMAP after v0.40 (2026-11-03): engine-direction talk (a build without Monomachine; the MM chord glitch first), slides on the sample and Machinedrum machines' own continuous controls, Octatrack-style rec trigs, then a comparison with heavylight's Capicola time-stretch. The roadmap also plans to read Aggregat (export DB, research map) before new DN2 work._

_Related: builds on `dn2-firmware-explore` (docs/CHANGES-FROM-UPSTREAM: forked dnfw at 8c40698); cites `elektron-firmware-tool` (README credits); uses tool `digikit` (README: checks or gates run in digikit's emulator (not shipped)) - see [PROJECT-FAMILIES.md](../PROJECT-FAMILIES.md)_

### digitone-2-modding-skill

Agent skill (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor; install with `npx skills add`) for developing Digitone II firmware mods: ColdFire MAIN OS patching in C, SHARC DSP audio code, verification in two emulators (digikit + a whole-DSP SHARC emulator), rebuild/re-sign/flash over USB. Encodes stock-firmware addresses, hook sites, the ColdFire-to-DSP frame format, free memory and "hardware rules the emulators cannot check, which each once silenced a real unit" - read on 2026-10-31 via SKILL.md and references/*.md (SKILL.md has 20 rules incl. whole 32-byte boot blocks, stock encodings only, no L2 above 0x200B0000, never read unwritten DDR, 2 MiB image / section 7 under 1 MiB, stop after two failed flashes; scripts include hwrules.py, shapecheck.py, encodecheck.py, bootblocks.py, sim.py/simc.py, cfmod.py, rpc_flash.py). Facts and rules are folded into hardware/devices/digitone-2-os111-reference.md and hardware/common/agent-workflow.md. Note: tree pages are blocked for our fetcher by robots.txt; the blob pages were readable. Examples: double_time (sequencer clock hook), track_trim (-6 dB on track 1). Needs Python 3.11+, dnfw, m68k GCC, digikit. MIT (digikit-derived files GPL-2.0), 2 commits, 10 stars. Overtone was built with it. Closest existing relative of this repo's hardware/ folder.

_Latest seen (2026-10-31, secondary directories): altstrument: main @ 84c8cd3 (2026-10-29), no tagged releases; brick-risk flag set ("flashing carries a known, documented risk of damaging the device")._

_Related: uses tool `digikit` (catalogue notes: verification in digikit); uses tool `dn2-firmware-explore` (README: prerequisite dnfw (container, signing, C builds)) - see [PROJECT-FAMILIES.md](../PROJECT-FAMILIES.md)_

### coldfire-rs

Rust stack for ColdFire V4e (MCF5441x): toolchain (rustc_codegen_gcc + libgccjit for m68k-elf), runtime, PAC generated from an SVD, and an Embassy HAL (GPIO, PIT, INTC, eDMA, UART, DSPI, eSDHC eMMC block reads, SSI/I2S, USB OTG device mode). Not an emulator and not an Elektron mod: the README never mentions Elektron or digikit, the only link is the topic tag "digitakt". It is relevant here because digikit names the MCF54415 as the control CPU of Digitakt II (and the Digitone II is described as ColdFire too). Drivers were run on the author's own MCF54415 board. README: API is young and may change before 1.0. 33 commits, Apache-2.0 OR MIT. Same owner also has deluge-sdk (Synthstrom Deluge, out of scope). Org shows no public members; no relation to ElekLabs/Em D found.

_Sources: GitHub README, FirestormAudio profile page_

### elekloader (simonjohansson fork - Digitakt II / Digitone II support)

GitHub says forked from elekloader/elekloader (not irpina's repo); 173 commits, GPL-2.0-or-later, NOTICE covers digikit code. Per README: Digitakt II 1.17 experimental - whole builds and linkable mods with their own core work, core checked in digikit's emulator, a key-swap mod works on a unit. Digitone II 1.12 experimental - whole builds, linkable mods, SHARC (DSP) mods and selectable synth/filter mods work; UI events and remote input checked on a unit, sine variants ran ten-minute note sweeps plus limited project/effects checks. Analog Rytm MKII 1.74 linkable mods with own core, builds with the core work on a unit; Analog Four MKII 1.56 hook bus, mod storage, unused DDR and recovery checked on a unit. Issue #13 plans Digitone II control-side support modelled on the Digitakt II implementation (hash-based stock-file recognition, devices/digitakt_mk2.py profile). 22 open issues.

### digi-roll-studio

Native Rust desktop sequencer for Digitakt II, Digitone II and Analog Four, built from digi-roll. Writes to hardware: README recommends throwaway projects. Safe-write ceremony of five rules (re-read and back up the destination pattern first, OS build on an allowlist, user confirmation, change only needed bytes, read back and byte-compare). Gen-2 dump protocol (digis) vs gen-1 (Analog Four). +Drive file-write commands 0x57/0x58/0x59 hardware-verified for a single chunk only, not called by the app (writes above 16 KiB refused); 0x5A/0x5B/0x5C (move/copy/delete) not implemented. Protocol code ported from elk-herd (BSD-2, (c) mzero). Fixtures: 34 real .syx dumps. 124 commits, GPL-3.0-or-later. Not firmware modding. Windows/Linux write testing incomplete.

_Related: vendors `elk-herd` (catalogue notes: protocol code ported from elk-herd) - see [PROJECT-FAMILIES.md](../PROJECT-FAMILIES.md)_

_Sources: GitHub README, search 2026-10-31_

### digitone-syx-toolkit

Python CLI (+ Tkinter GUI) to capture, replay, diff and hex-view SysEx, and to generate Digitone II PATTERN .syx from an empty template. README (Japanese) says Digitone II only. Hardware-validated: pattern-wide mode, tracks 1-8, steps 1-128, normal trigs, pitch, velocity, length (inherit/explicit/INF), tempo/speed/total steps, import/send. Not supported: chords, track-default rewriting, condition/probability/micro timing/retrig, non-destructive editing. Length encoding per README: inherit = 0xFF, explicit INF = 0x7F, finite 0x00..0x7E. 47 commits, licence not shown.

_Sources: GitHub README, SYXGRID README_

### DNX

Browser tools (Web MIDI, Chromium only, nothing uploaded) for Digitone and Digitone II projects: Expander (each sound-locked Digitone 1 sound gets its own track on the Digitone II), Manager (move/copy/swap/clear/rename patterns across banks with undo; Insights: polymeter, PATTERN RESET cost, voice use), Library (browse/search/rename the 2,048 +Drive presets; wavetables need Digitone II with "Waverider" firmware), Backup (whole +Drive into one .dnx with a manifest; excludes global settings), Probe (read-only identification and traffic capture) and CLI commands (project, plan, convert, copy, rearrange, rename, track, rebuild, diff, sheet; dry run by default). Write safeguards: WRITE switch must be armed, copy of current contents saved first, every write read back and compared, destinations checked against a fresh listing, never writes the loaded project, never converts a DN2 preset to DN1; close Transfer and Overbridge first (shared MIDI ports). Formats: .dnprj (DN1) and .dn2prj (DN2) projects, sound banks .syx; payloads LZ4-compressed inside a ZIP; SysEx uses 8-in-7 MSB-first. Author discloses LLM use; AGPL-3.0-or-later, TypeScript, 15 stars, created 2026-09-07. Not firmware modding. Report button opens a prefilled GitHub issue.

_Related: cites `libanalogrytm` (README: reference for Elektron structures); cites `digitone-syx-toolkit` (README: used as cross-reference / prior art); cites `elk-herd` (README: elk-herd as the model it follows); cites `digi-roll` (README: digi-roll reached the same write sequence independently; code not read) - see [PROJECT-FAMILIES.md](../PROJECT-FAMILIES.md)_

_Sources: elektronmods id 39, SYXGRID README_

### Elektron Emu

Five VST3 plug-ins (Mac, Windows) that run each machine's real OS in an emulated CPU: Digitakt II, Syntakt, Analog Rytm MKII, Digitone II, Model:Cycles. Firmware not included; the user places the .syx from Elektron's site in a per-machine folder. +Drive emulated and persisted; WAV loading on DT2, Rytm and DN2. Digitone II's DSP is compiled locally on first open (needs a C compiler, else a slow interpreter that renders offline only). Caveats: Rytm analog voices/effects are a custom model that does not sound like the real machine; Syntakt analog tracks 9-12 missing; Mac builds unsigned. 2 commits, 19 stars, no licence stated. Personal project, not affiliated with Elektron (panel photos belong to Elektron).

_Sources: GitHub README, altstrument tools page_
